extracted.intended_audience: vehicle manufacturers, seat suppliers, test laboratories, compliance engineers, and vehicle safety regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Federal rule amending FMVSS No. 210 test procedures for seat belt assembly anchorages, specifying force values, body block placement zones, and an optional Force Application Device (FAD) as an alternative compliance test device. Includes detailed design, positioning, and procedural criteria for certification testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchorage strength requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Seat belt anchorages must be sufficiently strong to remain attached to the vehicle structure in a crash; the standard requires anchorages to withstand specified forces when tested according to the test procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For lap-belt-only (Type 1) anchorages the required test force is 22,241 N (5,000 lb). For combination lap/shoulder (Type 2) anchorages the required test forces are 13,345 N (3,000 lb) applied to the lap portion simultaneously with 13,345 N applied to the torso (shoulder) portion. These forces are applied via pelvic and torso body blocks (or alternative FAD connection points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test force application timing and hold
rubrics_metrics.description: Test force must be attained and maintained according to specified timing requirements during the anchorage strength test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test force must be attained within 30 seconds and held for 10 seconds. Laboratory procedures include a preload prior to full test force (see preload criteria). Photographs and measurements of load application angles are taken while at the preload level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preload magnitude and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A preload is applied to the body blocks prior to application of the full test force for positioning and measurement purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratory test procedure specifies a preload equal to 10% of the test force. The SNPRM discussed a positioning preload of 1,335 N for zone placement (used for positioning verification in the proposed zone procedure). While at preload, target positions are verified and load application angles measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of failure (permanent deformation allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes failure of an anchorage under the test load is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent deformation or rupture of a seat belt anchorage or its surrounding area is not considered a failure if the required force is sustained for the specified time. The anchorage, attachment hardware, and attachment bolts must withstand the loading for the test duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard specifies shape, dimensions, and covering of the torso and pelvic body blocks used for testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMVSS No. 210 specifies the shape, dimensions, and the foam covering of the torso and pelvic blocks, but otherwise construction may vary. The torso and pelvic blocks are placed on the seat, secured with the seat belt, and attached to a force actuator to apply load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block placement zones (three-dimensional zones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule establishes allowable three-dimensional zones for positioning pelvic and torso body blocks on the seat prior to test force application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zones are based on NHTSA research (2018 report) and are specified so the origin of the torso/pelvic target lies within the applicable zone after preload. Zones were mathematically expanded from data across vehicle types to be applicable to a wide range of vehicles. Positioning is verified while a preload is applied (e.g., target must be within zone).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference points and zone boundary definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Zones and placement references are defined relative to seating reference points and manikin H-point conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zone boundaries reference vehicle-based points such as the seating reference point (SgRP) and other seat geometry conventions (e.g., forward transverse plane 100 mm forward of SgRP used in analogous FMVSS No. 222 procedure). H-point definitions and SAE practices are referenced for determining seat geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of zones across vehicle and seat designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Zones must be practicable and applicable to a wide range of vehicle types and seat configurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA evaluated factors affecting body block position across passenger cars, MPVs, trucks, buses, and heavy-duty vehicles; zones were chosen to be large enough to accommodate variability but modest in size to limit test condition variability. Considerations include integrated seats, narrow center seats, and seat restraint features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of zones and effect on variability/compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Zone size selection aims to reduce test variability without increasing stringency of the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA's research indicates zones are not expected to cause large variability in force vectors or test outcomes; the refined procedure reduces the set of permissible test conditions and thus reduces variability. If a vehicle fails in the zone but passed with an unusual placement outside the zone, failure is considered proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Force Application Device (FAD) optional compliance alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAD (FAD1 and FAD2) is specified as an optional alternative test device manufacturers may choose instead of body blocks for certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAD design drawings (two-dimensional engineering drawings) are incorporated by reference; NHTSA also provides three-dimensional design drawings for reference. Manufacturers can elect to certify using either body blocks (with zones) or the FAD.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD design details and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications and design aspects of the FAD are established to replicate occupant belt geometries and ensure consistent testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design considerations include durability and strength, material and potential belt slippage, weight (FAD1 weight specified as 55.8 kg / 123 lb in research), dimensions (FAD1 based on 50th percentile adult male contours), abdomen area, bridged pull yoke for lap-belt-only tests, clarifying attachment to the force actuator, human-form contouring, effect on seat back deformation, tolerance values, and availability of design drawings and supplemental 3-D data to facilitate fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rules for FAD1 versus FAD2
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to decide whether FAD1 or FAD2 is used at particular designated seating positions (DSPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA proposed using FAD1 unless testing in accordance with S4.2.4 (narrow seats). If FAD1s contact each other (prevent side-by-side fit), inboard FAD1s would be replaced with FAD2s progressively until contact is resolved according to the specified replacement order. The proposal clarifies when the contact check is made (prior to preload or prior to full test) in the final rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD test procedure: seating and attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: How the FADs are seated and connected for testing at the outset (pre-load seating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FADs are seated on the seat, secured with the seat belt(s), and attached to a force actuator with separate connection points on torso and lap portions for Type 2 belts. For lap-belt-only tests, a bridged pull yoke connects torso and lap connection points so they are jointly pulled. The test procedure specifies resting the FAD against the seat back, but does not require cinching it against the seat back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FAD on buses and heavy-duty trucks
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific consideration of FAD applicability and selection for large/heavy vehicle seating configurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments and testing addressed whether FAD2 should be used on buses and heavy-duty truck seats where FAD1 may not fit; NHTSA tested applicability across vehicle classes and considered specific seating geometries and constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeatability and equivalence with body blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration that test results using the FAD are repeatable and, where applicable, equivalent to results using body blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA conducted repeatability analyses and comparisons between FAD and body block results; the final rule states no evidence that FAD results in different compliance outcomes and provides manufacturers choice of device to mitigate concerns. NHTSA docketed studies including repeatability analyses (e.g., DOT HS 811 139).

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning procedure (for body blocks and FAD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed procedure for how test devices are positioned on seats before test force application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For body block zones: apply positioning preload, then verify block 'target' lies within specified zone. For FAD: seated at outset and secured; procedures clarify timing of checks for contact between adjacent devices and whether preload or post-preload checks determine device selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic and measurement documentation at preload
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to document load application angles and device positions while at preload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the preload is applied, photographs and measurements of the load application angles are taken to document initial positioning and establish reproducibility of test setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat adjustment and H-point considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Seat adjustment procedures and use of H-point/seating reference geometry in positioning and zone definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include seat adjustment state for testing, use of H-point (pivot center) and SAE J826/J1100 practices to define seating geometry and locate zone boundaries relative to SgRP and other reference planes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoulder belt height adjustment and D-ring considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for adjustable shoulder belt anchorages when positioning torso block or FAD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some vehicles have height-adjustable D-rings; positioning procedures and zone checks must consider the torso belt adjusted height (and school-bus analogous definitions) when determining torso block placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat belt pretension, routing, and use of dedicated test belt
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements/expectations on belt routing and pretension during tests and whether a dedicated test belt should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses belt pretension and routing as common issues; NHTSA addressed comments about whether a dedicated test belt should be required and how pretension/removal of slack is handled differently between FAD and body blocks (FAD sits on seat so slack removal is easier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Force application angle
rubrics_metrics.description: The angle at which the test load is applied to the belt/device must be measured and controlled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Load application angles are measured at preload and considered in analysis. The test procedure and zone positioning reduce variability in force vectors; measurement documentation is required during testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold time requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration for which the full test force must be maintained during the test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full test force must be held for 10 seconds after attainment within 30 seconds; hold time is part of the pass/fail assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing of side-facing seats
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability of the anchorage strength test to side-facing seats and any special considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMVSS No. 210 historically excluded side-facing seats (1970 amendment) but later rulemaking proposals addressed side-facing seats; the final rule discusses testing considerations for side-facing seats as part of 'issues common to FAD and body blocks.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory safety concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety of test technicians and laboratory operations when positioning devices and applying preload/test forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments raised laboratory safety concerns (e.g., supporting torso blocks during preload); NHTSA considered these in evaluating FAD vs. body blocks and in procedural clarifications aimed to reduce manual handling and improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing and potential recertification costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs associated with acquiring FADs, conducting tests, and potential recertification or redesign driven by the new procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA estimates cost of each FAD at approximately $8,000. Commenters raised concerns about testing costs and additional certification or redesign costs due to disharmonization; NHTSA discusses lead times and optional compliance choices to mitigate cost impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead time and compliance dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective date, incorporation by reference date, and compliance date(s) for manufacturers to meet amended procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule effective date: October 17, 2024. Incorporation by reference approved as of October 17, 2024. Compliance date: September 1, 2027, with optional early compliance permitted. Multi-stage manufacturers and alterers have an additional year to comply. NHTSA provided a two-year lead time for use of body blocks and the FAD as established by the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference and availability of drawings/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain design drawings and documents are incorporated by reference into the final rule and availability of supplemental 3-D data is provided for reference/fabrication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-dimensional engineering drawings of FAD1 and FAD2 are incorporated by reference. NHTSA is making three-dimensional design drawings available for reference purposes and docketed supporting material (FAD drawings and file locations) to facilitate fabrication and testing consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance options and regulatory alternatives / harmonization
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers have compliance choices and alternative procedures (domestic and international) were considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule allows manufacturers the choice to certify using body blocks (with zones) or the FAD, to address concerns about lead time and harmonization. Alternative solutions discussed by commenters include ECE R14 (6.3.4), Canadian Test Method 210, and FEA modeling; NHTSA evaluated these alternatives in the response to comments and regulatory alternatives sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference documentation and docketed research
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule relies on and references a body of docketed research, reports, and test data used to develop zones and FAD performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA docketed research reports (e.g., 'Development of Positioning Zones for FMVSS No. 210 Body Blocks,' repeatability analyses, and FAD test reports) which describe methodology, zone development, repeatability, and comparative testing. These materials are available in the rulemaking docket and referenced in the preamble.
